Transport lab 2: newer routes

More routes for getting a drawn element to another thread, document or device, using APIs from Chrome 130 to 160: WebRTC sender settings that keep text sharp, an RTCDataChannel moved to a worker, SharedArrayBuffer under Document-Isolation-Policy, WebTransport datagrams and Element Capture. The first lab has the other fifty.

Each row is a test that runs in this browser. Nothing runs until you press the button, and each row removes its canvas before the next one starts.

  1. source(): a drawable canvas with one element drawn into it.
  2. loopback(): two RTCPeerConnections in this page, joined to each other. It stands in for two devices.
  3. The worker that takes the data channel and reads the shared memory.
  4. The frame served with Document-Isolation-Policy.
  5. The freeze test.
  6. The timer that runs in a worker and in a SharedWorker.

          E · When the browser freezes the source tab

          A page that streams an element only produces frames while it runs. Chrome on Android freezes a hidden tab after about a minute; desktop Chrome does it under Energy Saver. This test measures what stops. Press the button, switch to another tab or app for at least 90 seconds, then come back.

          Findings

          • degradationPreference: 'maintain-framerate-and-resolution' keeps the element at its own size. With the default (balanced) and a low bitrate, WebRTC shrinks the picture, which blurs text first. With this value the encoder keeps the size and the page is responsible for sending fewer frames.
          • scaleResolutionDownTo sends a smaller stream without resizing the canvas. The source canvas stays at full size for the page; the phone gets a picture no larger than the size given.
          • An RTCDataChannel transfers to a worker, once, before anything is sent on it. Transfer it in the datachannel event. After that, input from the far device is parsed off the main thread.
          • Document-Isolation-Policy isolates one frame. The frame gets SharedArrayBuffer and Atomics.wait; the page around it stays as it was and keeps its cross-origin frames. This page isn't isolated, so the same code fails here, which the row before it shows.
          • WebTransport has no server on this site. The Cloudflare Workers documentation lists no way to accept a WebTransport session, so the datagram row fails with the browser's error. The row's code hasn't been run against a real server. Add ?wt=https://host/path to point the row at an echo server of your own.
          • Element Capture can't be answered by a headless browser, so those rows have only been run by hand. See the detail text they print.
          • Freezing hasn't been measured yet. Neither test browser can be made to freeze a tab (the DevTools lifecycle command changes nothing there, and no freeze event fires), so the freeze test above has only run with the tab visible. It needs a phone. The remote and cross-tab pages now report on their own page how long they were stopped.
          • track.stats doesn't exist on a canvas capture track. The frame counters are only on camera and screen capture tracks, so a canvas stream has to count its own frames.
